metadata.note: The San Francisco, Napa and Calistoga Railway and its predecessor and successor companies: the "Napa Valley Route", a 3,300-volt, 25 Hz AC electric interurban from the Vallejo ferry slip up the Napa Valley through Napa, Yountville and St. Helena to Calistoga, 41.6 timetable miles, connecting at Vallejo with the Monticello Steamship Company's boats to San Francisco. Drawn stage by stage from each stretch's own opening year: Vallejo - Napa 1905, Napa - Yountville 1907, Yountville - St. Helena 1 January 1908, St. Helena - Calistoga September 1912; all passenger service ended 12 September 1937. Mode is interurban (Rule 7): an electric line built to link separate towns.
metadata.ownership_note: Rule 4 splits, made where the company running the trains changed: (1) San Francisco, Vallejo and Napa Valley Railroad 1905-1911 (#C47AA8) - incorporated April 1902 as the Benicia, Vallejo & Napa Valley Railroad and renamed in 1906; a rename of the same corporation, so not split. (2) San Francisco, Napa and Calistoga Railway 1911-1935 (#8E2C6E) - a new company formed "for the purchase and operation of" the SFV&NV (OAC), so a split. (3) San Francisco and Napa Valley Railroad 1935-1937 (#5B1A48) - the 1935 reorganization of the SFN&C; JUDGMENT CALL: the trains kept the "Napa Valley Route" lettering and much the same management, but it was a new corporation running them, so it is split and given its own colour, which was checked to be absent everywhere else in data/. The month of each change is not sourced, so each split is at the calendar year.
metadata.colour_note: #C47AA8 and #8E2C6E were pre-assigned for this batch; #5B1A48 is new and appears nowhere else in data/.
sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco,_Napa_and_Calistoga_Railway - incorporation, rename, openings, 1913 wreck, AC electrification, 1937 end, 1938 excursion, 1938 track removal, Mare Island freight.

metadata.geometry_quality: Traced 42.0 mi Vallejo - Calistoga against 41.6 timetable miles (TT 38, 1924). By stage: Vallejo - Napa 15.3 vs 14.5; Napa - Yountville 8.8 vs 9.6; Yountville - St. Helena 10.0 vs 8.9; St. Helena - Calistoga 8.0 vs 8.6 (stage cut points are approximations of the station sites). Of the 42.0 mi: 9.5 hand-digitized from the 1916 USGS map on the railway's own alignment; 11.4 on the parallel Southern Pacific / Napa Valley Wine Train track (WRONG RAILROAD proxy, typically within ~100 m, with a post-1950s relocation through Yountville) and 4.7 on the adjacent abandoned SP Calistoga Branch grade; 14.5 on OSM street and highway geometry standing in for street running or roadside track (Vallejo, Suscol - Napa, Rutherford - St. Helena - Lodi Lane, Calistoga); 1.2 on the Washington St Bike Path; 0.7 straight line in two connectors (0.5 at Union, 0.2 at Calistoga). OpenHistoricalMap has no geometry for this railway (checked 2026-09-30), and OSM tags no way with it. No reversal or revisit artifacts (checked with the 120-degree / 350-m tests).
not_yet_sourced: The 1911 and 1935 changes of company are dated to the year only; the months are not sourced.
Calistoga opening year: 1912 (Napa Historical Society via Wikipedia, Register, golden-spike ceremony 12 Sept 1912) vs June 1907 (OAC finding aid) vs 2 Sept 1908 (trolleytuesdays). 1912 used.

Whether St. Helena - Calistoga kept passenger trains after the January 1932 carhouse fire (trolleytuesdays: restored 28 May 1932 to St. Helena only) and after 1936 (a Register summary: "until 1936"). Drawn to 1937.
Reorganization as the San Francisco & Napa Valley: 1935 (WRM, OAC, Wikipedia text) vs 28 May 1932 (trolleytuesdays). 1935 used.
The exact street route in Vallejo (the 1924 timetable names Sonoma & Georgia, Louisiana & Marin, Capitol & Branciforte) and the site of the Napa station.

The 1942 USGS Sonoma quadrangle (drawn after the line closed) shows a railroad labelled "Calistoga"/"Electric" running south from Union along the west side of Napa, west of Jefferson Street, which matches neither the Register's Jefferson Street route nor the 1916 map's Soscol Avenue approach. Unexplained; not used.
How far west of the SP the line ran between Rutherford and St. Helena ("behind the Rutherford school house").
Every headway except the 1924 ones; no other timetable was read. Official Guide issues of 1910-1937 would settle the earlier and later frequencies.
rule_notes: Rule 1: drawn to the last passenger train, 12 September 1937. The Mare Island freight (1919-1956), the Greystone - Barro freight spur the SP kept into the 1980s, and the 13 February 1938 one-day farewell excursion are not drawn.
Rule 5: electric from opening day - no animal-powered years.

Not drawn: the Southern Pacific's own steam Napa Valley branch, which this railway paralleled (a different railroad); the never-built Benicia end; the planned Lake County extension (poles set three blocks past Lincoln Avenue, never completed).

properties.speed_source: Measured from San Francisco, Napa & Calistoga employee Time Table No. 38, effective 20 April 1924: Calistoga-Vallejo, 41.6 timetable miles, in 98 min (No. 3, San Francisco Limited) to 107 min (No. 21, all stops) = 38-41 km/h; 39 km/h used. Applied unchanged to the other eras as an ESTIMATE - no other timetable was read.
properties.geometry_quality: Traced 15.3 mi from the Vallejo ferry (foot of Georgia St) to Third and Jefferson Streets, Napa, against 14.5 timetable miles Vallejo-Napa (TT 38, 1924: Vallejo MP 41.6, Napa MP 27.1); the Napa station's own site is not sourced, so the cut is at the downtown junction the route description names. Three kinds of geometry: (1) 9.5 mi Vallejo (Sonoma Blvd near Louisiana St) - Flosden - Collins - Napa Junction - Suscol HAND-DIGITIZED from the USGS 1:62,500 Mare Island quadrangle, 1916 edition, where this line is drawn as a railroad and labelled "San Francisco, Napa and Calistoga", parallel to and west of the Southern Pacific; the GeoPDF was georeferenced from its neatline corners, positional error estimated at 50-100 m. Today's California Northern / Mare Island track sits on or within ~100 m of the digitized line between Vallejo and Napa Junction but was not used. (2) 1.4 mi of Vallejo street running APPROXIMATED on today's Georgia Street and Sonoma Boulevard (OSM road geometry); the timetable's stop notes (a curve at Sonoma and Georgia, a stop at Louisiana and Marin, a crossing at Capitol and Branciforte) imply a street route that has not been resolved, so this 1.4 mi is a guess at the right streets. (3) 4.4 mi Suscol - Napa APPROXIMATED on today's Napa-Vallejo Highway, Soscol Avenue and Third Street (OSM road geometry), following the Napa Valley Register's description ("along Soscol Avenue, crossed the Napa River on Third Street, ... past the courthouse"); where the railway ran on its own strip beside the road, the road stands in for it. No straight-line legs.

segments.note: Opened Vallejo - Napa with a grand opening on 4 July 1905: the first electric interurban in the West to run on alternating current (3,300 V, 25 Hz). Built by the Hartzell brothers' company, incorporated April 1902 as the Benicia, Vallejo & Napa Valley Railroad (the Benicia end was never built) and renamed the San Francisco, Vallejo & Napa Valley Railroad in 1906 - a rename of the same company, so no split. Trains met the Monticello Steamship Company's boats to San Francisco at Vallejo. Ends 1911, when the San Francisco, Napa & Calistoga Railway was formed to buy and run the line. Headway is an ESTIMATE carried back from the 1924 timetable's ~90 min; no timetable from these years was read.
sources: Segment-level: the 4 July 1905 opening, the April 1902 incorporation, the 1906 rename and the 1911 successor company are from Wikipedia and the Napa Valley Register (Stockwell 2015); the OAC finding aid says the 1911 company was formed "for the purchase and operation" of the SFV&NV. The headway is NOT sourced.

segments.note: The San Francisco, Napa & Calistoga Railway took over in 1911 (formed to buy and operate the SFV&NV after the Calistoga extension left it unable to pay its contractors; James Irvine is named as the new principal). With the Monticello Steamship Company it sold through rail-and-boat tickets to San Francisco as the "Napa Valley Route". Time Table No. 38 (20 April 1924) shows 10 southbound trains a day Napa - Vallejo (6:42 a.m. - 9:20 p.m. from Napa), about one every 90 min; that 1924 figure is held across the whole era as an ESTIMATE. Peak ridership 615,351 in 1912; a head-on collision on 19 June 1913 killed 13. The Napa carhouse fire of 22 January 1932 destroyed three motor cars. Ends at the 1935 reorganization.

properties.geometry_quality: St. Helena (Main and Pratt) - Calistoga (Washington Street at Lincoln Avenue), traced 8.0 mi against 8.6 timetable miles St. Helena-Calistoga. 1.7 mi on SR-29 and Lodi Lane (OSM road geometry) following the Register's description ("parallel to the county road ... up to Lodi Lane. Then the tracks headed east toward the Napa Valley Railroad tracks"); 4.7 mi Lodi Lane - Calistoga on the abandoned SP Calistoga Branch grade (OSM railway=abandoned) as an ADJACENT PROXY - the USGS 1:62,500 Calistoga quadrangle (1927) draws the SP and this line through Bale, Larkmead and Dunaweal as one double-line symbol labelled both "Southern Pacific" and "S F N & C Elec.", i.e. side by side, so the drawn grade is the SP's but within the width of that symbol (~60 m); 0.2 mi STRAIGHT LINE from the SP grade to the east end of the Washington St Bike Path; 1.2 mi on the Washington St Bike Path, which is probably this railway's own approach (the Register: the tracks "veered west to approach Washington Street") but is not confirmed as such; 0.45 mi on Washington Street to Lincoln Avenue, the 1912 terminus (the 1913 depot was at Gerard and Washington).

segments.note: The Calistoga extension: right of way obtained 1911, first electric train into Calistoga 2 September 1912, formal opening with a golden-spike ceremony on 12 September 1912; terminus at Lincoln Avenue, Mission Revival depot at Gerard and Washington Streets completed 1913. SOURCE CONFLICT on the opening year: the Napa Historical Society (via Wikipedia) and the Register give 1912; the OAC finding aid says June 1907 and the trolleytuesdays summary 2 September 1908 - both earlier than the 1 January 1908 St. Helena opening the same sources accept, so 1912 is used. Headway counted from Time Table No. 38 (1924): 6 trains a day each way Calistoga - St. Helena; an ESTIMATE for other years.

segments.note: The San Francisco, Napa & Calistoga was reorganized in 1935 as the San Francisco & Napa Valley Railroad, still lettered "Napa Valley Route"; it went into receivership on 1 March 1936. Two new steel combines (Nos. 62-63, St. Louis Car, 1933) were among the last conventional interurban cars built in the US. When the San Francisco ferry connection ended, so did the passenger trains: last regular passenger trains 12 September 1937, last mail trains 30 September 1937; buses replaced them (sold to Greyhound in 1942). A farewell excursion ran Vallejo - Napa on 13 February 1938 for a railfan society and is NOT drawn. Freight to Mare Island continued, later as a Sacramento Northern subsidiary, until 1956 - not drawn (Rule 1). Headway is the 1924 figure carried forward as an ESTIMATE.

properties.geometry_quality: St. Helena (Main and Pratt) - Calistoga (Washington Street at Lincoln Avenue), traced 8.0 mi against 8.6 timetable miles St. Helena-Calistoga. 1.7 mi on SR-29 and Lodi Lane (OSM road geometry) following the Register's description ("parallel to the county road ... up to Lodi Lane. Then the tracks headed east toward the Napa Valley Railroad tracks"); 4.7 mi Lodi Lane - Calistoga on the abandoned SP Calistoga Branch grade (OSM railway=abandoned) as an ADJACENT PROXY - the USGS 1:62,500 Calistoga quadrangle (1927) draws the SP and this line through Bale, Larkmead and Dunaweal as one double-line symbol labelled both "Southern Pacific" and "S F N & C Elec.", i.e. side by side, so the drawn grade is the SP's but within the width of that symbol (~60 m); 0.2 mi STRAIGHT LINE from the SP grade to the east end of the Washington St Bike Path; 1.2 mi on the Washington St Bike Path, which is probably this railway's own approach (the Register: the tracks "veered west to approach Washington Street") but is not confirmed as such; 0.45 mi on Washington Street to Lincoln Avenue, the 1912 terminus (the 1913 depot was at Gerard and Washington).

segments.note: SF&NV era. Drawn to the end of all passenger service on 12 September 1937 (Wikipedia; a farewell run to Calistoga is reported for 1 October 1937). SOURCE CONFLICT: a trolleytuesdays summary says service resumed after the January 1932 fire with St. Helena as the terminus, and a Register summary says service to Calistoga continued "until 1936"; neither was confirmed, so this stretch may be drawn one to five years too long. Headway is the 1924 figure carried forward as an ESTIMATE.
